\chapter{Six More Signs Make Thank You Readable}
\label{ch:thanks-script-b}
\hlchaptermodality{3}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can write six more Devanagari signs from delayed or heard cues, then read and write dhanyavad independently.}

Hear, say, read, and independently write dhanyavad only after every load-bearing sign has been taught.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[da]{\mr{द} — dental da}

\label{lesson:MR-W03-da}



\begin{quote}
Keep the tongue-at-the-teeth position ready and add voice next.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script}
\begin{quote}
\mr{द}
\end{quote}

Keep the tongue at the teeth and add voice: \emph{da}. Descend the short stem; lift for the outer body, inward curl, and down-right tail; finish the headline.

\subsection*{Writing — delayed copy and retrieval}
Look at \textbf{\mr{द}} for five seconds, cover it, and write it once. Then retrieve the preceding three names: e-mark, anusvāra, dental \emph{ta}. Repair only one miss.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Deva-\%E0\%A4\%A6-order.gif}{Opiaterein, Devanagari da stroke animation}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[dha]{\mr{ध} — dha, voiced and breathy}

\label{lesson:MR-W03-dha}



\begin{quote}
Keep the dental voiced position ready; this sign adds breath.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script}
\begin{quote}
\mr{ध}
\end{quote}

Say \emph{da}, then add a puff: \emph{dha}. Curl around the upper spiral and sweep through its shoulder; lift for the lower bowl; descend the right stem; finish the headline.

\subsection*{Writing — delayed copy and a wider return}
Hide \textbf{\mr{ध}} after five seconds and write it once. Then, without models, name the first three signs of this runway: visarga, independent \emph{ā}, \emph{bha}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Deva-\%E0\%A4\%A7-order.gif}{Opiaterein, Devanagari dha stroke animation}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ba]{\mr{ब} — ba without the puff}

\label{lesson:MR-W03-ba}



\begin{quote}
Hold one hand near your mouth so you can notice the missing puff.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script}
\begin{quote}
\mr{ब}
\end{quote}

This is \emph{ba}, the quiet partner of \emph{bha}. Circle the oval body; descend the right stem; draw the inner diagonal down-right; finish the headline.

\subsection*{Writing — heard cue}
Cover the model. {[}YOU HEAR: \emph{ba}, without a puff.{]} Write the single consonant from sound alone. Uncover \textbf{\mr{ब}} and repair only the differing run.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Devanagari\_b\_\%E0\%A4\%AC.gif}{JackPotte, Devanagari ba stroke animation}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ya]{\mr{य} — ya}

\label{lesson:MR-W03-ya}



\begin{quote}
Say the first sound of English \emph{yes} once.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script}
\begin{quote}
\mr{य}
\end{quote}

Curve around the small inner curl; lift for the lower bowl; descend the right stem; finish the headline. The sound is the \emph{y} at the start of English \emph{yes}.

\subsection*{Writing — heard cue and retrieval}
Cover the model. {[}YOU HEAR: \emph{ya}.{]} Write the consonant once. Then say the three sign names immediately before it: dental \emph{da}, breathy \emph{dha}, quiet \emph{ba}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Deva-\%E0\%A4\%AF-order.gif}{Opiaterein, Devanagari ya stroke animation}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ḷa]{\mr{ळ} — Marathi's curled-back lla}

\label{lesson:MR-W03-lla}



\begin{quote}
Curl the tongue tip back once without adding a vowel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script}
\begin{quote}
\mr{ळ}
\end{quote}

Curl the tongue tip back for \emph{ḷa}. Draw the left loop through the centre and around the right loop in one run; add the short stem above the right loop; finish the headline.

\subsection*{Writing — heard cue and wider retrieval}
Cover the model. {[}YOU HEAR: curled-back \emph{ḷa}.{]} Write it once. Then retrieve the e-mark, anusvāra, and dental \emph{ta} by name; those three have now crossed a wider gap.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://indic-script-explorer.onrender.com/}{Indic Script Explorer, U0933 stroke data}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[va]{\mr{व} — between English v and w}

\label{lesson:MR-W03-va}



\begin{quote}
Relax the lips for a light sound between English \emph{v} and \emph{w}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script}
\begin{quote}
\mr{व}
\end{quote}

Marathi \emph{va} can sound lighter than English \emph{v}, toward \emph{w}. Travel left around the top and circle the loop counterclockwise; descend the right stem; finish the headline.

\subsection*{Writing — heard cue}
Cover the model. {[}YOU HEAR: \emph{va}.{]} Write one consonant from sound. Uncover \textbf{\mr{व}} and compare loop, right stem, headline.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Devanagari\_v\_\%E0\%A4\%B5.gif}{JackPotte, Devanagari va stroke animation}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[dhanyavād]{\mr{धन्यवाद} — now read what you already mean}

\label{lesson:MR-W03-dhanyavad-write}



\begin{quote}
Nothing in this word is an unknown shape now. Read \textbf{\mr{ध} · \mr{न्} · \mr{य} · \mr{वा} · \mr{द}}, join the middle consonants, and say \textbf{\mr{धन्यवाद}} — \emph{dhanyavād}, \textquotedblleft{}thank you.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item hear \emph{dhanyavād} and point to \textbf{\mr{धन्यवाद}}
  \item say the word from the English cue \textquotedblleft{}thank you\textquotedblright{}
  \item read \textbf{\mr{धन्यवाद}} without romanization
  \item cover every model and write \textbf{\mr{धन्यवाद}} from the heard cue
\end{itemize}

Then retrieve the last three signs separately: \emph{ya}, curled-back \emph{ḷa}, \emph{va}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stop after one independent attempt.
\end{tcolorbox}
